FirstPartyCoolDown.Prompt: (a) Determine whether R={(1,2),(1,4),(2,4)} is a function and justify. (b) For f(x)=x²−2x+1 find f(−1). (c) Is h(x)=x² one-to-one on x≥0? Justify using a formula or a horizontal-line sketch.
FirstPartyCoolDown.Expected: (a) No, input 1 maps to both 2 and 4. (b) f(−1)=1+2+1=4. (c) Yes on x≥0: the square function is strictly increasing there, so each nonnegative output has one domain input.

ScoreRubric.Criterion: Correctly identifies conflicting outputs for input 1
Computes substitution f(−1)=4 with intermediate steps
States why x² on x≥0 is one-to-one, including domain restriction
Explains vertical/horizontal line meaning or algebraic reasoning coherently

FirstPartyCoolDown.Evaluator: Teacher-led written response; do not auto-mark an unseen diagram or explanation.

LearningGoals: Determine from ordered pairs, tables, formulas and descriptions whether each input has a single output.
Use function notation to express and evaluate outputs and solve for valid inputs.
Determine whether an established function is one-to-one under its stated domain.
Interpret vertical-line and horizontal-line tests for graphs and implicit relations.
Identify basic toolkit function families and domain restrictions.
